Session · What happened (August 17)
The session focused on refining the architecture and implementation details for the Team Intelligence Agent and the RAG pipeline, with a strong emphasis on modularity, reusability, and proper system design. Key discussions revolved around the structure of the knowledge base, the ingestion pipeline, and the deployment of components to Quadrant Cloud.

Technical concepts discussed
*   **Team Intelligence Agent Capabilities**: Discussion on defining "intelligence" for the agent, focusing on inferring information humans struggle with or take too long to process, and the need for a locked persona and rules for generating comprehensive reports [17 August 2026, Page 2 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Knowledge Base Design**: Exploration of what constitutes the knowledge base, including entities like people, roles, tasks, projects, decisions, assignments, terminology, events, and facts, and how these will be structured and extracted from transcripts [17 August 2026, Page 1-2 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **RAG Pipeline Architecture**: Detailed breakdown of the RAG pipeline into three main systems: a vector store (for ingestion), a retrieval service (for experiments and reranking), and an evaluation system, with emphasis on making the reranker a separate, reusable module [17 August 2026, Page 7-9 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Normalization Layer**: The concept of a generic normalization solution for transcripts, moving away from hardcoded patterns to an extensible framework that can identify and transform patterns using LLMs [17 August 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Quadrant Cloud Deployment**: Practical steps for creating a cluster, obtaining API keys and endpoints, and connecting to Quadrant Cloud for storing embeddings and collections [17 August 2026, Page 14-17 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Context and Prompt Engineering**: The importance of separating context engineering and prompt building into distinct, reusable modules, rather than hardcoding prompts within Python files [17 August 2026, Page 9-10 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Training Profile**: The idea of building a daily updated training profile for each team member within the knowledge base, including name, thinking style, assigned tasks, and evaluation scores [17 August 2026, Page 2-3 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Assignments and actions
*   **Ganesh Krishna**:
    *   Change the ingestion pipeline to read from a shared database (like Supabase or Firebase) instead of local documents, but only *after* the normalization layer is deployed by the other team member [17 August 2026, Page 11-12 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   Develop a generic normalization solution that uses an LLM to identify and transform patterns in transcripts, rather than hardcoded patterns. Evaluate its performance on today's morning transcript [17 August 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   Design the V1 version of the knowledge base, specifically defining the JSON schema for the "training profile" which will include facts and observable events for each team member. This profile should be designed to be updated daily [17 August 2026, Page 2-4 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   Connect to GitHub MCP (or a shared GitHub repo for documents) to allow the Team Intelligence Agent to read code and information from all team members' repositories using their respective tokens [17 August 2026, Page 12-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   Build the pipeline for the knowledge base and show the first version or at least a design, ready to defend or brainstorm [17 August 2026, Page 13-14 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   Figure out the knowledge base design today and be ready to present it tomorrow, including whether it's a combination of Postgres and Quadrant, or only one of them [17 August 2026, Page 17 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Decisions
*   The Team Intelligence Agent will eventually generate large reports (e.g., 3000 tokens) and will need to leverage Ganesh's knowledge base to extract thinking and answering patterns, reducing the LLM's attention span burden from reading raw transcripts [17 August 2026, Page 2-4 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   The RAG pipeline will be structured into three main systems: a vector store (for ingestion), a retrieval service (for experiments), and an evaluation system [17 August 2026, Page 7-8 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   The reranker component within the retrieval service should be made a separate, reusable module to allow other components or experiments to utilize it independently [17 August 2026, Page 8-9 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   Configuration files should not be exclusively YAML; they can be JSON, XML, HTML, or even TXT files, as YAML is just a format [17 August 2026, Page 16 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   The shared documents for the team will be stored in a shared GitHub repository instead of MCP, and the Team Intelligence Agent will connect to this repo [17 August 2026, Page 12-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Important changes
*   The ingestion pipeline for all team members will eventually push normalized data into a common cloud-based database (like Quadrant) rather than local storage, making it a shared project [17 August 2026, Page 11 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   The approach to transcript normalization needs to shift from hardcoded patterns to a generic, LLM-driven framework [17 August 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   The Team Intelligence Agent's capabilities need to be re-evaluated and re-made from first principles to ensure it provides true intelligence beyond what Dakshinya's RAG can offer [17 August 2026, Page 4 — Siddharth Saminathan].

What you need to know or do
Your immediate next steps are to focus on designing the V1 of the knowledge base, specifically defining the JSON schema for the training profile that will track team members' progress and characteristics. Concurrently, you need to develop a generic, LLM-based normalization solution for transcripts and evaluate its effectiveness. Remember to hold off on changing your ingestion pipeline to read from the shared DB until the normalization layer is deployed. Be prepared to present your knowledge base design and the working normalization solution tomorrow.
